Privacy.title: Privacy Policy

Terms.title: Terms of Service
Terms.description: The terms for using Excellence AI. The service is an invitation-only enterprise workspace, not a public consumer chatbot.

Home.badge: Enterprise MCP server · Operated in the EU
Home.heroBody: Excellence AI is an enterprise MCP server: the secure, standard connection between AI tools and company systems. Your team keeps its familiar tools; you control access, approvals, and the audit trail.
Home.featureMcpBody: No new chatbot to roll out. Your team keeps working in the AI tools they know, while Excellence AI connects them securely to company systems.
Home.featureAccessBody: You decide who can access each company system. Sensitive actions only run after a human approves them.
Home.featureAuditBody: Every AI action is logged: who asked for it, which data was accessed, and what happened. Everything can be reviewed later.
Home.featureAdminBody: Company administrators manage AI agents, system connections, roles, and autonomy. Only approved capabilities are available.
Home.featureModelsBody: Claude, Codex, ChatGPT, Gemini, or Grok — your team uses what works. Company governance always stays in Excellence AI.
Home.howStep1Body: Who can use each AI tool and company system, and which actions require human approval.
Home.howStep2Title: The team connects its AI tools
Home.howStep2Body: One secure company MCP address. Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT, or any MCP-compatible client — the same connection.
Home.howStep3Title: A human decides at the sensitive points
Home.howStep3Body: File writes, folder creation, outbound actions: an approval card, one click.
Home.aboutBody: Excellence AI connects your team's AI tools to company systems. The company manages access, approvals, and audit in one place, while employees keep working in the tools they already know.
Home.aboutCardLead: <brand>Excellence AI</brand> is an enterprise MCP server operated by Excellence Pay Kft. It gives any MCP-compatible AI governed access to company systems — with a full audit trail, privacy safeguards, and human approval.
Home.aboutCardRest: The service is a closed, invitation-only enterprise workspace, not a public chatbot. External account connections are always optional; see the <privacy>Privacy Policy</privacy> and <terms>Terms</terms> for details.

skills.title: Skills
skills.body: A skill is a written workflow: it tells the AI teammate how to do a recurring job. On its own it cannot act — what it can actually do depends on the permissions given to the agent.
skills.hint: Every change starts as a proposal (proposed), and only becomes live (active) after approval — you can always roll back to an earlier version.
skills.migrateHint: If you just pulled new code, run the migration (npx prisma migrate deploy), then restart the dev server.
skills.needOperator: Viewing skills requires at least operator access.

menuAccess.title: Who sees which menu
menuAccess.body: Set which menu items and submenus each role sees in the header. By default everyone sees the full menu for their role — hide items that are not part of that role’s daily work.

GetStarted.title: Work in your favourite AI tool
GetStarted.body: Connect the platform to Hermes, Codex, Cursor, Grok, Claude, or Goose. Pick your app and follow the short install steps.
GetStarted.step1Body: You can use the same server address in every app.
GetStarted.codexBody: Paste the command into the terminal. Browser sign-in opens; use the same account you are using here.
GetStarted.cursorBody: The button opens Cursor and offers to install the server. Then sign in in the browser.
GetStarted.cursorFallback: If the button does not work, you can add the MCP URL above by hand in Cursor settings.
GetStarted.grokBody: Paste the command into the terminal. On first connect, sign in in the browser with your platform account.
GetStarted.grokHint: In Grok you can also open sign-in via /mcps → server → i.
GetStarted.claudeDesc: Add a connector in the app
GetStarted.claudeBody: Open Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector. For the name enter: {name}, for the URL paste:
GetStarted.claudeAfter: Then sign in with the same account you are using here.
GetStarted.claudeCodeBody: Paste the command into the terminal, then complete the sign-in Claude Code offers.
GetStarted.claudeCodeHint: This command is for Claude Code. For Claude Desktop use the guide above.
GetStarted.gooseDesc: Remote MCP extension in the app
GetStarted.gooseStep1: Open the Goose sidebar, then choose Extensions → Add custom extension.
GetStarted.gooseStep2: For type, choose the Streamable HTTP remote extension.
GetStarted.gooseStep3: For the id enter: {name}; for the name: Excellence AI. The server URL is:
GetStarted.gooseAfter: Click Add, then sign in with your platform account in the browser that opens.
GetStarted.step2Body: Open the connected AI tool and ask: “Who am I, and what AI teammates do I have?” If your teammates appear, the connection works.
GetStarted.reopenHint: You can reopen this page from the header at any time.
GetStarted.hermesDesc: Every AI coworker becomes its own Bot with a single request
GetStarted.hermesIntro: In Hermes Desktop every AI coworker gets its own Bot, with its role and skills. The Bot works through the platform, so you see and approve the work here and no passwords are stored on your machine. No plugin needed: stock Hermes is enough.
GetStarted.hermesStep1Body: Download it from the official site (version 0.21.5 or later) and start it.
GetStarted.hermesStep2Body: On first start Hermes asks which AI model to use and for its key. You can also set it later in the terminal:
GetStarted.hermesStep2Hint: Bots receive only this provider's key. Your other keys stay in the default profile.
GetStarted.hermesStep3Body: Paste the command into a terminal. A browser opens: sign in with the same account you use here.
GetStarted.hermesStep3Hint: Keep the server name “excellence”: Bots reach the platform under this name. To check the connection, run: hermes mcp test excellence
GetStarted.hermesStep4Body: In the Hermes chat (default profile), type:
GetStarted.hermesStep4Hint: Hermes creates a Bot for each AI coworker you can access. For each Bot a browser opens once for approval: sign in and accept.
GetStarted.hermesStep5Body: Open Bot Mode. Each coworker shows up as its own Bot, and you can start working in its chat right away.
GetStarted.hermesUpdateBody: If a coworker's role or skills change on the platform, its Bot tells you. Then type the same sentence again in the default profile. Your Bots' chats, avatars and settings are kept.
GetStarted.hermesApprovalHint: Anything a Bot would change (for example sending an email) waits here, on the platform, for your approval.

Provisioning.fromTemplateHint: Pick from the template catalog — the connector takes the template name.
Provisioning.customConnectionHint: No template — custom onboarding from discovery or a document.
Provisioning.usesTemplateName: Name: {name} — we use the template name, you do not need a separate one.
Provisioning.step1Body: Pick the type first. From a template the connector takes the template name; you only name a custom connection.
Provisioning.step2ApiBody: The public API description link is required; a key only if the partner API asks for one. After create, the wizard walks you through link approval, partner trust, looking for updates, and taking the first version.
Provisioning.accessKeyHint: Only needed if the partner API asks for a key. It stays in a secure secret store; it never goes into the database. Leave empty for a public, keyless API.
Provisioning.capabilityOnSync: We download the capability list on the wizard’s “Look for updates” step.
Provisioning.catalogHelp: If the link is a catalog (several API descriptions), you can pick which ones become connections.
Provisioning.singleApi: This is a single API description — create it with the “Create connector” button below.
Provisioning.catalogLeaves: Catalog index ({count} API descriptions) — pick which ones become connections:
Provisioning.sharedKeyHint: One key (e.g. a POSnavigator pn_ key) for every selected API. Each connection gets it in its own secret slot — you can replace them one by one later.
Provisioning.perLeafKeyHint: A separate key can be entered under each selected row.
Provisioning.noKeyHint: For public APIs that do not ask for a key.
Provisioning.itemCreated: {name} created — link approval and trust are still pending.
Provisioning.dualControlHint: The link usually needs another colleague’s approval before we go live — so we do not read from a mistyped or fake address. A platform superadmin can approve and activate alone. The wizard steps are the same as under Details on the card.
Provisioning.step3LinkBody: Check that the partner API description address is correct and from a trusted source.
Provisioning.step4TrustBody: We only download and activate API changes for a partner marked as trusted.
Provisioning.trustAlready: ✓ The partner is already marked as trusted.
Provisioning.step5SyncBody: We download the partner OpenAPI description and build a proposed capability list for the first live version.
Provisioning.versionAlready: ✓ A taken-over version already exists — the connection can be used.
Provisioning.step6ApplyBody: Review the first capability list. Until you approve it, the connection cannot be assigned to an agent.
Provisioning.step2TemplateBody: {name} — set the auth mode and required fields. The connector takes the template name.
Provisioning.templateSelfContained: The template builds a self-contained draft config from provider metadata and instance fields.
Provisioning.driveOauthNeeded: The Google Drive template needs the platform Drive OAuth setup (Platform · Settings → Google Drive OAuth).
Provisioning.googleApiOauthNeeded: The Google Analytics / Search Console / Ads templates need the platform Google API OAuth setup (Platform · Settings → Google Analytics / Search Console / Ads).
Provisioning.step2CustomBody: The flow takes you to a config candidate. You only create the draft in the next step.
Provisioning.openapiHint: Upload a spec or paste a URL
Provisioning.fromDoc: Generate from an API document (provisioning assistant)
Provisioning.fetchStepBody: Enter the public OpenAPI or API-doc URL. The platform downloads it, you review the content, then the provisioning assistant generates a config candidate.
Provisioning.reviewOrUpload: Step 2 — review or upload a file
Provisioning.onlyOpenApi: OpenAPI JSON/YAML only. We do not extract config from free-text docs right now.
Provisioning.truncated: (truncated — the full spec was too large)
Provisioning.manualDescriptorHint: Paste the JSON, or load the example, then continue to review.
Provisioning.secretNeverHere: The secret NEVER goes here, only the alias name intended for Secret Manager.
Provisioning.secretOnActivate: The credential secret is entered at activation (managed secret store).
Provisioning.materializerHint: The materializer validates fields on the server, then calls the same draft gate.
Provisioning.templateScopeSuper: Choose platform- or workspace-level. Saving creates a new version and runs the materializer self-check.
Provisioning.templateScopeTenant: The template goes into your workspace catalog. Saving creates a new version and runs the materializer self-check.
Provisioning.templatesFromThese: You can create a connector from these templates.
Provisioning.pendingHintMixed: For OpenAPI connections, link approval, partner trust, or taking the first version is still pending. Open the card for the steps.
Provisioning.pendingHint: Link approval, partner trust, or taking the first version is still pending. Open the card for the steps.
Provisioning.gapsHint: These connections are active in the database, but have no provisioning draft or self-updating card (often a migration or old seed leftover). They may still be assignable to an agent; if they are unused, decommission them — audited archive, not a hard delete.
Provisioning.unmanagedHint: There is no management UI for this row on this page — only decommission or platform support (if it needs to go back to a draft/OpenAPI path).
Provisioning.decommissionGapBody: Not a hard delete: after removing agent assignments and the managed secret-ref, the connection becomes archived. Bank-preset / L2–L3 needs a second approver.
Provisioning.reasonGapPlaceholder: E.g. migration leftover, unused http_api connection
Provisioning.confirmDecommNamed: Sure? “{name}” will be torn down and archived.
Provisioning.confirmDecomm: Sure? The connector will be torn down and archived.
Provisioning.sensitivityTitle: We found a sensitive pattern in the content (e.g. email, national ID, tax number).
Provisioning.sensitivityBody: By default only a local model could process it — but API docs often contain dummy/example data. If you are sure it is not real sensitive data, you can continue with an external model.
Provisioning.pendingOp: Waiting because an operation is in progress.
Provisioning.catalogNoSolo: This is a catalog index — create the connections with the leaf picker above; a standalone “Create connector” cannot run here.
Provisioning.fillRequired: Fill in the template’s required fields.
Provisioning.needConfig: Generate or provide a config descriptor first.
Provisioning.needDocUrl: Enter the API-doc or OpenAPI URL.
Provisioning.fileTooBig: The file is larger than 2 MiB.
Provisioning.onlyOpenApiFile: Only an OpenAPI JSON/YAML file can be uploaded.
Provisioning.invalidJson: The config is not valid JSON.
Provisioning.invalidTemplateJson: The template descriptor is not valid JSON.
Provisioning.pickTenantForTemplate: Choose a workspace for a workspace-level template.
Provisioning.needAtLeastOne: Pick at least one API description from the list.
Provisioning.needLeafNames: Give every selected row a name.
Provisioning.catalogNotSoloCreate: This is a catalog index — a standalone connection cannot be created from it. Use the “Create selected connections” button above.
Provisioning.sensitiveFound: We found a sensitive pattern in the document. If it is dummy/example data, you can continue with the button.
Provisioning.openapiExtracted: OpenAPI spec detected — config candidate extracted deterministically. Review it, then create the draft.
Provisioning.docFetchedTrunc: Document downloaded (truncated because of the size limit). Check the content, then generate a config candidate.
Provisioning.docFetched: Document downloaded. Check the content below, then click Generate config candidate.
Provisioning.fileLoaded: File loaded. Check the content, then generate a config candidate.
Provisioning.singleNotCatalog: This is a single API description, not a catalog index — you can use the plain “Create connector”.
Provisioning.catalogFound: Catalog index: {count} API descriptions in it. Pick which ones become connections.
Provisioning.batchAllOk: {count} connections created. You still need to approve the links and partner trust on the panel before you can look for updates.
Provisioning.batchPartial: {ok}/{total} connections created — see the failed rows below.
Provisioning.createdNeedLink: Connection created — the link still needs approval.
Provisioning.draftFromTemplate: Draft connector created from the template.
Provisioning.trustFailed: Marking the partner as trusted failed.
Provisioning.trusted: The partner is marked as trusted.
Provisioning.openapiLive: The OpenAPI connection is active and usable.
Provisioning.templateSaved: Connector template saved as a new version.
Provisioning.autoApproveOn: The workspace allowed limited automatic take-over.
Provisioning.autoApproveOff: Automatic take-over is off for the workspace.
Provisioning.activateKeylessBody: You did not enter an API key or a valid secret reference. Activate without a key anyway? Agent calls will fail auth until then.
Provisioning.activateKeylessShort: You did not enter an API key or a valid secret reference. Activate without a key anyway?
Provisioning.configUpdated: Config updated — validation/review/sandbox reset, run the gate again.
Provisioning.deleteNeverActivated: Permanent delete — only for a connector that was never activated. The broken connector and draft row are deleted; this cannot be undone.
Provisioning.reopened: Connector reopened as a draft — edit it, then activate again.
Provisioning.egressAdded: Egress host added to the allowlist: {host} — revalidated.
Provisioning.oauthSecretPlaceholder: Client secret of the OAuth app registered with the provider
Provisioning.rawKeyPlaceholder: Raw key generated in the external system
Provisioning.oauthSecretHint: The client secret goes into the managed secret store (secret-ref). The key is stored encrypted and never lands in the database.
Provisioning.rawKeyHint: Enter only the raw key — the system adds the “Bearer " prefix (for the bearer scheme). The key is stored encrypted and never lands in the database.
Provisioning.clientIdPlaceholder: client_id of the OAuth app registered with the provider
Provisioning.agentOwnedKey: Enter a key → this agent gets its own key
Provisioning.reasonActivePlaceholder: E.g. misconfigured egress host, replaced provider
Provisioning.editResetsGates: Saving resets the gate: validation, review, and the sandbox test will all run again before the connector can be activated.
Provisioning.unreadableConfig: The stored config cannot be parsed.
Provisioning.cannotEditLive: An active connector’s config cannot be rewritten live. To fix it, reopen as a draft: the connector goes offline (the Tool Broker will not resolve it), then you must walk validation→review→sandbox→activation again. Agent assignments stay, and return on reactivation.
Provisioning.deleteDraftBody: Permanent hard-delete — only for a never-activated draft. The broken draft connector and draft row are deleted for good (the delete is audited).
Provisioning.warningsFixable: Some of the warnings can be fixed in the draft config. After the change the gates restart, so the new config must be validated again.
Provisioning.newEgressHosts: New egress host(s) — add them to the allowlist before activation (§9, audited admin act):
Provisioning.notValidatedYet: The draft is not validated yet. Run the validator before sandbox test, review, or activation.
Provisioning.reviewBody: Final human approval that also considers the sandbox test. This gate only makes sense in draft. On an active connector you need revoke or a new version, not a later review rewrite.
Provisioning.sandboxBody: A narrow, non-live probe call. Activation stays blocked without a successful test.
Provisioning.activatePrereqs: Activation requires: non-failed validation, a successful sandbox test, and an approved review.
Provisioning.gmailOauthOk: The platform Google OAuth app is configured — Client ID and Secret are not needed at workspace level.
Provisioning.gmailOauthNeed: The Gmail connector uses the platform Google OAuth app. Before activation a platform admin must set it on Platform · Settings → Google OAuth.
Provisioning.driveOauthOk: The platform Google Drive OAuth app is configured — Client ID and Secret are not needed at workspace level.
Provisioning.driveOauthNeed: The Google Drive connector uses the platform Drive OAuth app. Before activation a platform admin must set it on Platform · Settings → Google Drive OAuth.
Provisioning.googleApiOauthOk: The platform Google API OAuth app is configured (Analytics / Search Console / Ads) — Client ID and Secret are not needed at workspace level.
Provisioning.googleApiOauthNeed: The Google Analytics / Search Console / Ads connector uses the platform Google API OAuth app. Before activation set it on Platform · Settings → Google Analytics / Search Console / Ads.
Provisioning.existingSecretHint: If you already store the secret elsewhere, reference it here instead of typing a key. Accepted forms: env:NAME, secret-manager:projects/…/secrets/<id>, secret-ref:<id>. Otherwise leave empty and type the key above.
Provisioning.badAlias: Alias form not accepted. Use an env:, secret-manager:, or secret-ref: prefix — or leave empty and type the key above.
Provisioning.actingUser: Acting user email (registered in the CRM — X-Acting-User header)
Provisioning.actingUserNeeded: A CRM-registered acting user email is required for the keyed test.
Provisioning.addToOauthApp: (add it to the OAuth app settings)
Provisioning.keylessWarn: You can activate without a key, but we ask for confirmation — the agent will not call successfully until then.
Provisioning.assignToAgent: Assign to an agent (human admin act)
Provisioning.perAgentKeyHint: (agent_owned — optional if you use the connector’s shared key)
Provisioning.decommissionActiveBody: Not a hard delete: after removing agent assignments, recomputing those agents’ http_api capabilities, revoking active user grants, and deleting the managed secret-ref, the connector becomes archived — the connector row and audit history stay. The act cannot be undone (you would have to activate again). Bank-preset / L2–L3 needs a second approver.
Provisioning.httpApiViaEditor: This connector was set up through the “API connector” editor (http_api runtime config).
Provisioning.oauthClientId: OAuth client ID (not a secret → config)
Provisioning.fromTemplateShortHint: Pick from the template catalog — the connector takes the template name.
Provisioning.customShortHint: No template — custom onboarding from discovery or a document.
